correctness.rationale: The all-iteration survivor is a compact expanding interval Markov repeller; each closed graph walk uniquely determines a periodic point. Integer boundary orbits are either zero or nonperiodic and escaping, hence no cyclic overcount. Group rows of the unit-branch adjacency are exactly identical, yielding trace and Sylvester determinant identities for a size-r integer quotient. An increasing positive Perron vector and a uniform ratio estimate imply 0<lambda_r-m_r<=1/2. Solving the last three eigenvector equations and bounding the earlier tail gives lambda_r=m_r+1/3-4/(135m_r)+O(m_r^-2). The explicit second-period formula follows by exact summation. value.rationale: The countable expanding Markov map has natural four-adic levels, and cutting at each level yields a compact invariant subsystem. Its all-period point inventory and exact entropy are genuine dynamical invariants, not arbitrary slices. The theorem gives a constructive determinant reduction from 4^r to r dimensions and a sharp second-order cutoff spectral correction measuring the extra successor link. This is a complete natural family of exact quantities, beyond a generic rationality observation or finite enumeration, with plausible use in quantitative approximation of countable-state dynamics.
